I’ve been pretty strict with what I eat—usually under 800 calories a day. I bring a protein bar and black coffee to work, and that’s about it. I work on elevators all day, climbing shafts, so I figure I can handle it. But my mom keeps saying I’m too thin, and my doctor wanted me to gain weight, which I just don’t get—she’s exaggerating. I look fine. Actually, if I’m being honest, I still think I need to lose a few pounds.

I avoid anything with sugar or fat like the plague. If I eat a high-calorie food, I panic—I genuinely believe I’ll gain weight overnight. That’s why I measure everything and check labels obsessively. I organize my meals in this strict order: same time, same portions. Sometimes I won’t eat if I can’t control exactly what’s in it.

I know it looks like I’m obsessed, and yeah, I do these routines with food, but it’s not random. It’s because I can’t let myself get fat. My body *has* to stay this way. It’s not about the food itself—it’s about not becoming someone I hate in the mirror.
D021-D016_h024.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D021-D016_h025.question:
I’ve always cared about being healthy, but over the past year, I’ve become really focused on making sure I don’t gain weight. I’m a social worker, so I’m used to being tuned in to emotions, but this feels different—I can’t stop thinking about how certain foods might make me gain weight, especially carbs and fats. I know my body needs nutrition, but the idea of eating them makes me so anxious I can’t do it. I weigh myself multiple times a day, and if the number goes up even a little, I’ll skip meals or do extra cardio until it goes back down.

I’ve noticed I feel dizzy a lot, and I haven’t had my period in nearly a year. My hair has been thinning too, but I don’t see these as red flags—just side effects of being disciplined. I’m not afraid of food because it’s “contaminated” or because I have to eat in a certain order—it’s because I’m terrified of getting bigger, of losing control over how my body looks. That fear is always in the front of my mind, shaping every bite I do or don’t take.
D021-D016_h025.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
